customManagers.description: Update ARGs annotated with '# renovate: datasource=… depName=…'. The Dockerfiles compose their FROM refs from a registry variable and a digest-pinned tag, which the dockerfile manager cannot replace; tag and digest are captured separately so digest-pinned ARGs stay managed.

Local checks run the CI toolchain images by tag outside any workflow file. Managing them here keeps release-check and docs-site-check on the image CI uses; the update shares the workflow's branch because the dependency name is the same.
Composite actions take their BuildKit, SBOM scanner and binfmt images as `with:` strings, which the github-actions manager does not read. Tag and digest are captured so the digest stays managed.

The local MCP end-to-end compose file runs the Authentik that the nightly mcp-e2e job runs through Harbor's ghcr proxy. Naming the dependency after the workflow's image puts both pins in one update, so one pull request moves both; the proxy serves the upstream digest.
See the Authentik manager above: the compose file's Postgres moves with the nightly job's Postgres from Harbor's Docker Hub proxy.
The local agent image is tagged with the OpenCode version it carries. The example configurations and the live guide name that tag, so they move with the opencode group.

The agent sandbox warm pool and the live local example run the released unfold-agent image. Renovate moves them to the newest candidate the release pushed to Harbor, so they do not depend on a release commit to follow the release.
The landscape build loads Mermaid and Marked from jsDelivr inside Playwright.

Unfold depends on a released Ploeg (system ADR-0039). apps/unfold/ploeg-release.json pins Ploeg's contract bundle, an OCI artifact on GHCR, by version and digest; scripts/ploeg-contract.py unpacks it into apps/ploeg after checking both digests.

packageRules.description: The annotated-ARG manager owns the composed base images and the opencode pin.
Bare versions are reused outside the FROM line; digests are captured explicitly.

Forgejo-resolved workflow pins keep the CI-only commit shape. The org forgejo overlay sets it too, but as runner-level config it is applied before the preset's per-update-type commit types, which then win.

The agent image and the mise pin must move together: one OpenCode version is what the workbench, the probe and the image share. The npm package names no repository, so Renovate cannot find its release notes by itself; naming the source puts them in the pull request, where the person merging and the Run that explains the update (Ploeg ADR-0106) read them.

Every Unfold release is a candidate X.Y.Z-rc.N, so the released unfold-agent image is offered as one. Moving the references releases nothing: a releasing commit type would cut a candidate whose image Renovate then offers again. A reference ahead of Harbor is a release still publishing, not one to roll back.

engines ranges are compatibility floors, not dependencies. Pinning or bumping engines.vscode narrows which VS Code builds the extension installs on, and engines.node is the deliberate Node 24 line. Both move by hand.
vsce refuses to package when @types/vscode is newer than engines.vscode (^1.99.0). Raise this bound together with engines.vscode.
Unfold's chart image tag is empty on purpose: the release train fills it from appVersion. Renovate would otherwise digest-pin it.

Ploeg's release workflow opens the Ploeg pull request by running scripts/consume-ploeg-release.sh (ADR-0041), so Renovate leaves the contract bundle pin, the Go module and the Unfold chart's ploeg dependency alone (ADR-0043): two writers on one pin would race. The weekly ploeg-behind check fails when the pin falls behind Ploeg's newest release.
These pins replace the copies npm bundles in the agent image, and the patch script accepts only the bundled major. Raise the bound when npm bundles a newer major.
See the undici rule: brace-expansion is pinned to npm's bundled major.
Node types follow the Node 24 runtime that mise, engines and the images pin.
@astrojs/check and typescript-eslint accept TypeScript up to 6. Lift this when both peer ranges include 7.
three is vendored into apps/unfold/public/vendor/three (Unfold ADR-0028). A version bump alone breaks the vendored copy's checks; upgrade by hand with npm run vendor:three.
uv runs every docs gate, and a 0.x minor may break: uv 0.13 made Python 3.15 the default (dependency intake of #351). A person reviews each 0.x minor before it merges.

pnpm 11 and later keep the pnpm that packageManager names in the lockfile's first document (packageManagerDependencies), and a frozen install refuses a lockfile whose record disagrees. The self-hosted Renovate image runs its own global pnpm, which switches to the packageManager version with package-manager management turned off, so that record keeps the old version (#593, fixed by hand in #596). Corepack runs exactly the pnpm packageManager names, as CI does, and that pnpm rewrites the record. The homelab's allowedCommands must list this command; docs/operations/ci-troubleshooting.md has the entry.
